text: In 1886, Coca-Cola sold nine servings of its drinks per day in its first year; now it has over 2.2 billion servings consumed daily worldwide, which is about 25,500 every second.
During conversations, each speaker's turn averages 2 seconds with a 200-millisecond pause in between. This quick transition is nearly universal across cultures.
On June 4, 1923, jockey Frank Hayes suffered a fatal heart attack mid-race, but his horse, Sweet Kiss, finished and won, making him the only jockey to win a race posthumously.
Two diseases have been successfully eradicated: smallpox in 1980 after the last case in 1977, and rinderpest in 2011 after the last case in 2001.
The difference between mist and fog comes down to visibility: if you can't see farther than 0.6 miles (1 km), it's fog; if you can, it's mist.
According to the FDA, Kraft Singles are labeled as "pasteurized prepared cheese product" due to containing under 51% real cheese.
Perfluorohexane dissolves large amounts of oxygen, allowing animals to survive underwater by inhaling oxygenated liquid.
In the 1870s, 37 cats were trained to deliver mail in Liège, Belgium, but the experiment was short-lived due to inefficiency, with most cats taking up to a day for deliveries.
In 1889, Margherita pizza was crafted to honor Queen Margherita, using ingredients that symbolize the Italian flag's colors: tomato, mozzarella, and basil.
Nestlé produces KitKat and Rolo globally, with the exception of the U.S., where these products are manufactured by their competitor, Hershey's.
Dexter Holland, lead singer of The Offspring, earned a Ph.D. in molecular biology from the University of Southern California, graduating in May 2017 while still active in the band.
Shakira was turned down by her school choir in second grade, with her teacher criticizing her strong vibrato as sounding "like a goat."
Approximately 2,000 thunderstorms occur worldwide at any given time, totaling around 16 million annually.

From 1777 until its admission to the United States in 1791, Vermont existed as a self-governing independent state. It had its own copper coins and operated its own postal service.
Warren Buffett said in the 2017 HBO documentary "Becoming Warren Buffett" that he eats McDonald's every morning, choosing one of three items that never cost more than $3.17.
Will Smith owed $2.8 million to the IRS and almost went bankrupt just before signing the contract for "The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air."
The Indonesian slang word "jayus" refers to a joke that is so poorly delivered or unfunny that it becomes amusing.
On March 30, 1867, the U.S. bought Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million, using a Treasury check for payment.
After turning 65 in Arizona, a driver's license must be renewed in person every five years and includes a mandatory vision exam.
President George H. W. Bush banned broccoli from being served on Air Force One and at the White House because he simply did not like the vegetable.
The longest unbroken alliance in world history is between England and Portugal. It has lasted since 1386 and still stands today.
Grant Wood's 1930 painting "American Gothic" depicts a father and daughter, not husband and wife, as is commonly believed.
When Facebook acquired Instagram for $1 billion in April 2012, the company was just 18 months old and had 13 employees.
During the first iPhone presentation in 2007, Steve Jobs had to switch between several iPhones to prevent crashes due to limited RAM and unstable software.
On August 25, 2010, a plane in Congo crashed due to panic caused by an escaped crocodile, resulting in 20 deaths and two survivors, including the crocodile.
Joe Arridy, who had an IQ of 46, was called the "happiest prisoner on death row" and entered the gas chamber smiling; he was later found to be innocent.
Chipotles aren't a separate chili pepper species. They are simply red, fully ripened jalapeños that have been smoked and dried.
The "Lord of the Rings" costume team spent three years linking plastic chain mail. Each Orc suit had 13,000 rings and took approximately three days to assemble.
Non-violent prison escapes in Mexico aren't criminally charged, as they acknowledge the natural human instinct to seek freedom.
Some of the oldest dice ever discovered were found at Skara Brae in the Orkney Islands of Scotland. Used between 3100 and 2400 BC, they were carved from bone, often from sheep or cattle.
A study at Florida State University found that "Portal 2" improves cognitive skills more effectively than brain-training games like Lumosity.
In 1872, President Ulysses S. Grant was arrested for speeding in a horse-drawn carriage and had to pay a $20 fine.
The word "hello" was only used as a greeting following the invention of the telephone. Before that, it was merely a word to get someone's attention.
The King of Macedon threatened to raze Sparta, saying "If I bring my army into your land, I will raze your city." The Spartans replied: "If." No attempt was made to capture the city.
90% of all Americans live within ten miles of a Walmart store.
Although the TV show "Friends" is based around life in New York City, the entire show was filmed in California.
The average NFL career lasts approximately three years, and nearly 80% of players experience financial difficulties within three years of retirement.
At Wimbledon, line judges are trained to recognize swearing in various languages due to the tournament's strict no-swearing policy.
Cumulus clouds, known for their fluffy appearance, actually weigh about 1.1 million pounds on average.
